Avoid creating unnecessary GLContext on DrDC thread

On Android, the GLContext is never used on DrDC thread (no WebGL/Video).

Update shared code, mainly in SharedContextState and shared image to
allow null GLContext and associated classes like gles2::FeatureInfo.

Added SharedContextState::GetMaxArrayTextureLayers (next to existing
GetMaxTextureSize)

Update webview and drdc init code to not create GLContext when not using
GL, behind a feature.

[wdspec] Fix BiDi detached node and preload script order WPTs

- Fix flaky failures in WebDriver BiDi detached-element input tests and
  missing assertion in preload script ordering tests.
- Detached DOM nodes returned without strong ownership can be garbage-
  collected before input commands check them, and test_script_order
  compared the console text without an assert keyword.
- Request result_ownership="root" for detached nodes and assert the
  first console message in test_script_order.

Cancel pending PDF translation when Reading Mode is closed

PDF translation is kept in a pending state until Reading Mode finishes distilling the page content. If the Reading Mode side panel is closed before the translation begins, cancel the pending translation state so that it does not trigger while Reading Mode is closed.

Auto-dismiss ephemeral contextual tasks button after inactivity

Introduces the kContextualTasksEphemeralButtonAutoDismiss feature flag,
which automatically dismisses the ephemeral contextual tasks toolbar
button and disassociates its task after a configurable period of
inactivity.

When the contextual tasks side panel is closed, a timer starts for all
tabs associated with the task. If the panel is reopened, the timers are
canceled. If the timer expires, the button is hidden, the associated
tabs are removed from eligibility, and the task is disassociated. Also
adds about:flags entries and interactive UI tests.

Make resolver failure deterministic in ResolveFourAddresses test

ResolveFourAddresses expects resolving "unknown" to fail, but its host
mapping rules only cover the successful lookups. The error case can
therefore depend on the machine's resolver configuration. Map "unknown"
to ^NOTFOUND so the test exercises ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED without
consulting the underlying resolver. Preserve the existing success,
error, pipe-disconnection, and outstanding-request checks.

Add CompositeValue and CompositeGenerator to ui/decoration

Introduce CompositeValue<Specs...> and CompositeGenerator<Details...> in
ui/decoration/decoration_details.h to combine multiple DecorationDetails
types into a single cached ninebox image around a shared content rect.

- CompositeValue<Specs...> holds an std::optional<Spec> for each part
  so any subset of parts can be omitted while sharing a single cache
  type.
- CompositeGenerator<DecorationDetails<Specs, Generators>...> combines
  each active part's margins with MinInsets(), aperture insets with
  MaxInsets(), and paints each active part in template argument order.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for Glic Tab Managers

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

Bug: b:501142609
Doc: go/miracleptr-in-containers

[cbor] Build map entries directly in a vector in Reader::ReadMapContent

Valid canonical CBOR maps already arrive in strictly ascending
Value::Less key order. Instead of inserting every entry into an
intermediate std::map (incurring O(N log N) comparisons, per-node heap
allocations, and a final node-extraction pass), append entries directly
to a std::vector<std::pair<Value, Value>> after checking against the
last inserted key, and binary-search existing keys only on the error
path to distinguish DUPLICATE_KEY from OUT_OF_ORDER_KEY.

This change contains no intentional observable behavioral changes.

[content] Fix NavigationEntryScreenshotTest for Auto SyncToken

This CL is a follow-up of https://crrev.com/c/8518437 and a prerequisite
before enabling the UseAutomaticSyncTokenManagement feature.

When the UseAutomaticSyncTokenManagement feature is enabled (in the
future), SyncTokens are managed internally by ClientSharedImage and
client-visible SyncTokens become empty. As a result, some tests in
NavigationEntryScreenshotTest which expect non-empty SyncTokens will
fail. To fix this, the current CL changes the test expectations. As a
supporting change, this CL also adds a GenSyncTokenCHROMIUM()
implementation needed for ClientSharedImage::GenSyncTokenInternal().

Exclude WPAD auto-detect from ProxyConfigMonitor::IsProxyConfigured()

ProxyConfigMonitor::IsProxyConfigured() previously checked
net::ProxyConfig::HasAutomaticSettings(), which returns true when either
auto_detect() or has_pac_url() is set.

On Windows, "Automatically detect settings" (WPAD, fAutoDetect = TRUE)
is enabled by default in Windows Internet Settings on fresh OS installs,
which populates config.set_auto_detect(true) in ProxyConfigServiceWin
even when no proxy or WPAD server exists on the network. This caused
~91% of Windows connections to be bucketed into WithProxy in
PrivateAi.Client.HandshakeFailedErrorCode2.*.

Replace config.HasAutomaticSettings() with config.has_pac_url() so that
IsProxyConfigured() only returns true when an explicit proxy is
configured (manual proxy rules, an explicit PAC script URL, proxy
override rules, or dynamic routing rules).

CONV=c68a678f-02d0-4b00-bf09-1f9aefa17407

[SG Android] Enable EnableProxyOverrideRulesForAllUsers on Android

Previously, the EnableProxyOverrideRulesForAllUsers policy and the
corresponding affiliation checks in ProxyOverrideRulesPolicyHandler and
PrefProxyConfigTrackerImpl were only enabled on Linux, macOS, and
Windows.

Enable the EnableProxyOverrideRulesForAllUsers policy and its backing
kEnableProxyOverrideRulesForAllUsers preference on Android as well. This
allows Android builds to support user-level proxy override rules and
affiliation checks controlled by this policy, and prepares the
preference for use by ProxyProvisioningDomainsPolicyHandler.

[iOS] Show Site Info for permissions when Page Tools is unavailable

When IsDomainLevelSitePermissionsEnabled() is true, tapping the
permissions infobar banner or the omnibox permissions badge
unconditionally opens the Page Tools sheet. However, Page Tools is not
always available (when IsPageActionMenuEnabled() is false or in
Incognito when IsChromeNextIaEnabled() is false).

This CL routes the permissions infobar action and the omnibox
permissions badge (including the overflow badge menu) to open the Site
Information page via showPageInfo() when Page Tools is unavailable.

Re-enable mixed-content object-tag, img-tag and imageset WPTs

top.http-rp/opt-in/object-tag.https.html and
top.meta/unset/img-tag.https.html now pass: upstream WPT commit
39a9cbddfe03f dropped the timing-out swap-scheme <object> redirect
subtests and regenerated the img-tag test to expect auto-upgrades.
Remove their stale expectations.

imageset.https.sub.html predates Mixed Content Level 2 autoupgrades.
<img src="http://..."> is now upgraded to https://, so pointing it at
the plain HTTP port made the upgraded load fail its TLS handshake.
Use the HTTPS port (same technique as common.sub.js's
*-http-downgrade cases) and expect the upgraded https:// URL to load.

<picture><source srcset> and <img srcset> are blockable and are not
upgraded. Blocked fetches still produce a resource timing entry, with
transferSize 0, so assert that those entries show no download
(rather than that no entry exists), and that no upgraded https://
request was made.

[a11y] Stop dirty-descendant propagation at already-dirty ancestors

This change reduces Blink accessibility CPU time by 2.08% and overall
renderer main thread (`CrRendererMain`) CPU time by 0.46% in Speedometer
3. Specifically, it reduces CPU time in
`AXObject::SetAncestorsHaveDirtyDescendants` by 93.25%.

Previously, marking an accessibility object as having dirty descendants
always walked all the way to the root node. It also walked the ancestor
chain a second time to verify the result. Now, Blink stops walking
upward when it reaches an included ancestor that already marks its
descendants as dirty. Blink also skips redundant parent updates when
inserting a newly initialized child. This change does not alter
accessibility behavior.

[iOS] Fix background scan upload failure

The upload for asynchronous scanning the download file is failing
because the file is being moved out of the sandbox to the user selected
location before the upload finishes. This CL creates a temporary
directory and uses the APFS Copy-on-write `clonefile` to avoid
duplicating bytes while preserving the original file name and extension.
And as soon as the scan complete, the scanner is deleted, and the
temporary folder with the file is deleted on the scanner destruction.
Added a scheduler on startup to clean up the "tmp/enterprise_scan"
folder as a failsafe measure.

Also added a local feature flag so that if clonefile is failing, we can
shut it down.

spanification: Make zucchini::CalculateCrc32() take a base::span

CalculateCrc32() took a [first, last) pair of raw pointers. Iterating
over it needed pointer arithmetic, and every test case in
crc32_unittest.cc needed UNSAFE_TODO.

It now takes a base::span<const uint8_t> and loops over it with a
range-based for loop. Callers pass their ConstBufferView directly,
which converts implicitly to a span. The tests use a std::array and
build their sub-ranges with first() and subspan(). The DCHECK death
test for a reversed range is removed, because a span cannot represent
a reversed range.

capture_mode: Allow overriding recommended folder with Downloads

When ScreenCaptureLocation is configured as a recommended policy,
selecting the default Downloads folder in the Capture Mode settings menu
calls SetUsesDefaultCaptureFolder(true), which sets
kUsesDefaultCapturePathPrefName to true.

Previously, CaptureModeController::GetCurrentCaptureFolder() checked
policy_path.enforcement == CapturePathEnforcement::kRecommended outside
the !pref_service->GetBoolean(kUsesDefaultCapturePathPrefName) branch.
As a result, when kUsesDefaultCapturePathPrefName was true, execution
skipped the custom path check and fell through to the recommended policy
check, returning policy_path.path instead of the default Downloads
folder.

Move the kRecommended check inside the
!pref_service->GetBoolean(kUsesDefaultCapturePathPrefName) block so that
an un-overridden recommended policy is still used by default, while
explicitly selecting Downloads overrides the recommended policy folder.

WebMCP: Unify imperative and declarative tool unregistration

Before this CL, we had both:
 - `ModelContext::UnregisterImperativeTool()`; and
 - `ModelContext::UnregisterDeclarativeTool()`

... because they had different contracts: unregistering a "missing"
imperative tool was a bug, so we could CHECK() in that case, whereas
unregistering a missing declarative tool was expected due to some form
state management bugs. Those bugs are fixed in
https://crrev.com/c/8581732, so this CL unifies the two paths to share
the same, strict, unregistration method.

This CL introduces no behavior change.

R=mfoltz

f4d07e489f1593506d0162a483412102065c405d [ diff ] 
WebMCP: Keep a form's declarative tool in sync with its registration

`HTMLFormElement` holds an `active_webmcp_tool_` that it later
unregisters from its document's `ModelContext`. But it could hold onto a
tool that is not registered in two ways:

1. When `ModelContext::RegisterDeclarativeTool()` silently rejects
   registration, the form kept the tool anyway because `ModelContext`
   never made the form aware of registration failure.
2. A currently-being-removed form's
   `ScheduleDeclarativeWebMCPToolRegistration()` method returned early
   for documents without a frame. This means a form can keep a handle
   to the tool it originally registered, while its window/document are
   inactive. If the form was then adopted into another, active document,
   then it might act on that document's `ModelContext`, but with the
   old tool.

This CL establishes the invariant that `active_webmcp_tool_` is non-null
iff it is registered with the `ModelContext` of the form's document:

 - `RegisterDeclarativeTool()` returns whether the tool was registered,
   and the form drops its tool if not. As a result, a later mutation of
   a rejected form retries registration.
 - The frame and sandbox checks no longer short-circuit the
   unregistration path, so a form always unregisters its tool when it
   can no longer be a tool, including from a frameless document.
 - `UnregisterDeclarativeTool()` now `CHECK()`s that the tool is
   registered, and like `UnregisterTool()`, only notifies the browser
   when the document is active.

The guard in the last point mirrors https://crrev.com/c/8578418, which adds the same IsActive() check to the imperative UnregisterTool() path. There, the inactive-document unregistration is reachable from script by aborting a tool's AbortSignal after its iframe is removed. Here, it only becomes reachable because of the second point: before this CL, a form in a frameless document returned early and never unregistered, so UnregisterDeclarativeTool() never ran for an inactive document. Now that it can, it needs the same guard, since the inactive document's ModelContextHost remote has been reset.

R=mfoltz

[infra] Run mac-webdriver-bidi-rel tests on bare metal, not on VMs

The WebDriver BiDi E2E tests start a new browser for each test. On the
Mac VMs (VirtualMac2,1, 5 cores, no GPU, no display) the browser start
stalls for minutes at a time. One stall fails 10 to 20 tests in a row
with a 20 second timeout, and a retry with 5 attempts of 40 seconds
still fails. The VMs also have no GPU, and screenshot tests hang in
Page.captureScreenshot after a scroll.

Every build since the move to the builderless pool needed the retry
step, and builds 311 and 312 failed outright:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac-webdriver-bidi-rel/311/overview
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac-webdriver-bidi-rel/312/overview

Tryjob 59 reproduced a 200 second browser start stall on
mac-1314-h526--vm1:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/try/mac-webdriver-bidi-rel/59/overview
https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/task?id=7b5c9a2c64c5fe10

Replace the mac_26_vm_optional mixin with mac_26_arm64, like
chromedriver_py_tests and blink_web_tests on mac-arm64-rel. The tests
now run on the bare-metal Mac-26 arm64 pool.

spanification: Use OPENSSL_memdup for RSA-OAEP label copy

Replace the OPENSSL_malloc() + UNSAFE_TODO(memcpy(...)) used to copy
the RSA-OAEP label in rsa_oaep.cc with a single OPENSSL_memdup() call.
BoringSSL owns the copy, so it still has to be allocated with the
OpenSSL allocator. OPENSSL_memdup() does the allocation and the copy
in one step, which removes the unsafe memcpy.

The copy is now checked for allocation failure, and ownership is
released only after EVP_PKEY_CTX_set0_rsa_oaep_label() succeeds, since
BoringSSL takes ownership only on success. This fixes a leak when the
call fails.

Also drop the <string.h> and base/compiler_specific.h includes, which
are no longer used, and add the missing <vector> include.

Run content-security-policy/xslt WPTs in virtual/xslt-enabled

XSLT is disabled for web tests via fieldtrial_testing_config.json, so
ProcessingInstruction::CheckStyleSheet() bails out before the XSL
stylesheet is fetched, no CSP check happens, and these tests time out
waiting for a securitypolicyviolation event. The XSLT tests were
consolidated into the xslt-enabled virtual suite, but
external/wpt/content-security-policy/xslt was never added to it.

Add the directory to virtual/xslt-enabled, where
xslt-strict-dynamic-blocked.html and xsltprocessor-include-blocked.html
pass (verified 10/10 locally). Move the base xslt-strict-dynamic-blocked
Timeout into the centralized XSLT-disabled block.
document-function-blocked.html still times out with XSLT enabled
(crbug.com/440374744) and keeps its inherited Timeout expectation.

[OTP] Replace MockSmsOtpService with FakeSmsOtpService.

Tests of `SmsOtpService` clients used `MockSmsOtpService` or a real
`SmsOtpServiceImpl`, which was either driven by ad-hoc mocks and fakes
of `SmsOtpBackend` or had no backend at all. This CL introduces
`FakeSmsOtpService`, which lets tests simulate the arrival of SMS OTPs
and platforms without SMS OTP support, and inspect active subscriptions
and pending `RequestOneTimeToken()` calls. All of these tests now use
it:
- `MockSmsOtpService` is deleted.
- `SmsOtpServiceImpl` is no longer used by tests of its clients, and
  `SmsOtpBackend` is now only mocked by `SmsOtpServiceImplTest`.
- `TestAutofillClient::set_sms_otp_backend()` and `GetSmsOtpBackend()`
  are removed. Tests inject the fake via `set_sms_otp_service()`.

Test-only change.

parent
75bfde3f491d0be06ba764086325f1303e7bd5e8 [ diff ] 
libdisplay-info: Switch to Autoroll

libdisplay-info is a pristine git submodule pinned to an upstream
release tag, with no checked-in files derived from the upstream version.
pnp-id-table.c comes from hwdata's pnp.ids, not from libdisplay-info, so
rolls don't change it. That makes it a good fit for the Skia Autoroller,
which updates DEPS and README.chromium's Version and Revision.

Roller configuration (requested separately):
  Mirror: external/gitlab.freedesktop.org/emersion/libdisplay-info
  Tag regex: ^upstream/(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$

linux-wayland-mutter-rel is already triggered by changes to
third_party/libdisplay-info, so CQ catches breakage. The expected manual
work is adding new upstream source files to BUILD.gn.

Also point License File at upstream src/LICENSE instead of a checked-in
copy (which was identical), as wayland does. The Chromium license check
can fail to resolve checked-in copies for autorolled dependencies, and
reading the license from the rolled revision keeps it from going stale.

c-v: Guard scroll anchor reset with CanDirtyStyle

NotifyPriorityScrollAnchorStatusChanged was originally only called
inside if (CanDirtyStyle())

Commit e9ce5a60247f2 inadvertently moved that call outside the if
(CanDirtyStyle()) block.

When a size container needs layout, style recalc for its subtree is
deferred until layout. Calling NotifyPriorityScrollAnchorStatusChanged
during this deferred style recalc clears the ancestor scroll anchor
mid-layout before NotifyAfterLayout can restore the scroll offset.

[iOS][TTC] Use ttc::ToolResponse in TtcActuationHandler

TtcActuationResponse was an iOS-only struct that duplicated the shared
ttc::ToolResponse contract. Callers also had to manually invoke
validation before dispatching an actuation request.

Replace TtcActuationResponse with ttc::ToolResponse and
ttc::ToolResponseCallback across TtcActuationHandler. Add
ProcessToolCall to validate an incoming ttc::ToolRequest and dispatch the
resulting action proto in a single step.

[Search Hijacking] Add SearchIntegrity metrics for DSE set by policy

Adds two boolean UMA histograms to SearchIntegrity (along with their
`.Enterprise.` variants for managed profiles) recorded once per profile
at startup when the default search engine has `policy_origin` set to
`kDefaultSearchProvider` (`CreatedByDefaultSearchProviderPolicy()`):

- `Search.Integrity{Enterprise}.IsDefaultSetByPolicyInLowTrust`:
  Records whether a policy-attributed default search engine is active in
  a low-trust management environment, where the higher of the platform
  (for policy loading) and profile management authority trustworthiness
  is below `ManagementAuthorityTrustworthiness::TRUSTED`.

- `Search.Integrity{Enterprise}.IsDefaultSetByPolicyWithoutMatchingPolicy`:
  Records whether a policy-attributed default search engine is active
  when `default_search_provider_data.template_url_data` has neither an
  active mandatory (`IsManaged()`) nor a recommended
  (`GetRecommendedValue()`) non-disabled policy dictionary with a
  matching URL.

[SafetyFRE] Move carousel page logic to a mediator

SafetyPromoCarouselCoordinator previously handled both UI initialization
and business logic.

Key changes:
- Add SafetyPromoCarouselMediator. It owns the page logic: it sets the
  page count, follows the selected item and handles the page the user
  swipes to (onPageSnapped). It only writes to the model and doesn't
  touch views.
- ACTIVE_PAGE_INDEX now also drives the RecyclerView: the binder calls
  SafetyPromoCarouselView.setActivePage(), which moves the page
  indicator and scrolls to the page. Both cached views are bound to the
  model, so a hidden view keeps its page and the manual
  scrollToPosition() calls in the coordinator go away.
- The coordinator keeps view inflation, caching and configuration
  changes, and forwards the snapped page from its scroll listener to
  the mediator. Its public API is unchanged.
- Add SafetyPromoCarouselMediatorUnitTest for the page logic, and drop
  the coordinator tests that covered it. The coordinator tests now use
  a mock mediator, except for two that run the real one to check that
  cached views keep the active page across layout switches.

[paint-timing] Record histograms for unique contentful paint counts

Today, PerformanceEntries for paint timing are only emitted when there
is a new LCP candidate or when Element/Container Timing is opted in. To
understand the upper bound on how many PerformanceEntries would be
generated on typical pages if every contentful paint were reported, this
CL counts the number of unique paints that produced any new image or
text paint timing records in PaintTiming::MarkPaintTimingInternal()
(including initial paints of visible images or text, elements removed
and re-added to the DOM, and text repaints after user interaction
tracked for soft navigations).

UMA histograms are recorded once per committed HTML/XHTML document
(excluding initial empty documents), split by outermost main frame vs.
subframe (`.Subframe`):
- Renderer.PaintTiming.ContentfulPaintCount{FrameType}.BeforeInputOrScroll:
  recorded on the first user input or scroll (or when the page is first
  hidden or the document context is destroyed if no input or scroll
  occurred).
- Renderer.PaintTiming.ContentfulPaintCount{FrameType}.UntilPageHiddenOrContextDestroyed:
  recorded when the page is first hidden or the document execution
  context is destroyed.

Update profile unit tests in ['ios/chrome/browser/enterprise/data_controls', 'ios/chrome/browser/enterprise/identifiers', 'ios/chrome/browser/enterprise'].

In Chrome on iOS, there is only one personal profile and any additional
profile must be a managed profile associated with a managed identity via
AccountProfileMapper.

TestProfileIOS::Builder::SetName() and enforces that
TestProfileManagerIOS::AddProfileWithBuilder() is only used once to

  hardcoded default profile names.

  profile and managed profiles explicit.

Android: Use smaller batches for browser tests

Browser tests run each test in its own process, and the host-side
timeout for a batch is a fixed 10x --shard-timeout (1200s) regardless of
batch size (up to 256 tests). On debug emulators (e.g.
android-16-x64-dbg-tests) tests average ~8.5s, so batches of ~140 tests
hit the timeout and whichever test happens to be running is reported as
a failure.

Cap browser test batches at 64 tests.

mutter, glib, gvdb: Switch to Autoroll

With the previous CLs, mutter and glib no longer check in files that
change with every release, so a point release only needs a DEPS bump,
which an autoroller can do. gvdb has no generated files at all. Switch
all three from Manual to Autoroll.

New major versions of mutter, and new minor versions of glib, still
need manual work (BUILD.gn source and codegen-input updates). As
documented for Skia Autoroller dependencies, the roll will fail CQ and
the owner takes over the roll CL. The READMEs describe what to do.

Also point mutter's and gvdb's License File at upstream's src/COPYING,
as wayland does, instead of checked-in copies (which were identical).
Reading the license from the rolled revision keeps it from going stale.
A missing license file (e.g. without checkout_mutter) is only a warning
in README.chromium validation.

glib's src/COPYING has the same terms, but is a reformatted copy of the
LGPL 2.1 that the Chromium license check doesn't recognize ("Extra:
LGPL-2.1"), and upstream doesn't have a copy with the standard
formatting. So glib's checked-in LICENSE is replaced with the standard
text (identical to the copies in libgudev and gsettings-desktop-schemas,
which pass the check). It doesn't change when glib is rolled.

Verified by simulating point-release rolls in reverse: with only the
DEPS revisions changed to mutter 51.0 and glib 2.90.0, everything builds
(with the version headers following automatically) and the
representative interactive_ui_tests pass with --use-mutter.

Roller configuration (requested separately):
  mutter: external/gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/mutter
    Tag regex: ^upstream/(\d+)\.(\d+)$
    (skips the 51.alpha/51.beta/51.rc pre-release tags)
  glib: external/gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib
    Tag regex: ^upstream/2\.(\d*[02468])\.(\d+)$
    (odd minor versions, e.g. 2.89.x, are development releases)
  gvdb: external/gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gvdb
    Branch upstream/main (no release tags), with roll_cooldown: 2w

mutter: Generate code at build time instead of checking it in

Generate mutter's enum types (glib-mkenums), clutter marshallers
(glib-genmarshal) and D-Bus code (gdbus-codegen) at build time with the
in-tree glib's code generators, using the templates from
//third_party/glib/codegen.gni, instead of checking in the output of
on_update.sh. This removes 38 generated files, including the unused
meta-dbus-x11.{c,h}.

The arguments and input lists match upstream's meson.build files (taken
from meson's generated build commands), and the mkenums header lists are
in upstream's order. glib_mkenums and glib_genmarshal gain an
input_base_dir option that runs the tool in a given directory, so input
paths in the generated #include directives and comments match
upstream's include paths (e.g. "clutter/clutter-enums.h"), as
on_update.sh's sed post-processing did before.

config.h stays checked in, as a template (config.h.in) with VERSION and
PACKAGE_VERSION filled in at build time from src/meson.build
(configure_version_header.py), as glib now does for its config.h.
meta-default-modes.h also stays checked in, since its generator runs the
host's /usr/bin/cvt (from the xcvt package) to calculate VESA CVT display
mode timings. on_update.sh now only produces these two files.

With this, a mutter point release only needs a DEPS bump. A new major
version still needs BUILD.gn updates (sources and codegen inputs).

All 36 files generated at build time, and config.h, are byte-identical
to the previously checked-in files, even though the checked-in files
were generated with the host's glib 2.88 tools and these are generated
with the in-tree glib 2.90 tools. on_update.sh reproduces the remaining
two files unchanged.

Tested: built mutter and ran TabDragging DragInSameWindow,
DetachToOwnWindow and DragAll, BookmarkBarViewTest1/2,
BrowserFocusTest.ClickingMovesFocus and TabsRememberFocus, and
KeyboardLockInteractiveBrowserTest.RequestedButNotActive* with
--use-mutter.

[TabStateStore] Add regression tests for restore and tracking lifecycle

Add unit regression tests for TabStateStore and
ModelTrackingOrchestrator covering restore and tracking lifecycles:
- Authoritative loadState() + restoreTabs() does not duplicate
        registration observer or full saves.
- Non-authoritative shadow catch up updates tab count tracker
        for both regular and incognito models.
- clearState() followed by loadState() and restoreTabs()
        initializes restoration and tracking cleanly.
- Post-restore tab registrations save tabs and update tab
        counts.
- Authoritative restore does not re-save existing tabs if data
        was already loaded.
- Incognito cipher factory loading before or after restore
        triggers full save and tracking.

Test: TabStateStoreUnitTest

79eca365a23cc62b697ffeb5b53d6d19215bd34f [ diff ] 
glib: Fill in the version in config.h and glibconfig.h at build time

config.h and glibconfig.h come from meson's host configuration checks
and stay checked in, but they also contain values derived from the glib
version (GLIB_{MAJOR,MINOR,MICRO}_VERSION, GLIB_INTERFACE_AGE,
GLIB_BINARY_AGE, PACKAGE_STRING and PACKAGE_VERSION), so they changed
with every glib release, including point releases.

Check them in as templates (config.h.in and glibconfig.h.in) with those
values replaced by placeholders, and fill them in at build time from
src/meson.build (configure_version_header.py), using the same formulas
as upstream's meson.build. on_update.sh produces the templates, and
fails if filling them in doesn't reproduce meson's output exactly, so
a change to upstream's formulas or a new version-dependent value is
caught when glib is updated rather than producing wrong values. With
this, the checked-in files only change when upstream changes its
configuration checks, and a glib point release only needs a DEPS bump.

config.h is now generated into a private include dir, since it is only
used by glib itself; previously the checked-in copy was on glib's public
include path.

The generated config.h and glibconfig.h are byte-identical to the
previously checked-in files, and on_update.sh reproduces the templates
unchanged.

[Password Manager] Dedupe password saving policy check

passwords_section.ts and settings_section.ts had identical copies of
computePasswordManagerDisabled_(). The name was also misleading: the
check doesn't mean Password Manager is disabled. It's true only when a
mandatory admin policy turns off credentials_enable_service, which
blocks saving new passwords. Recommended policy and values set by
extensions don't count.

Move the check into prefs/policy_utils.ts as
isSavingNewPasswordsBlockedByMandatoryPolicy() and rename the property
to passwordSavingBlockedByPolicy_. The computed properties now depend on
prefs.credentials_enable_service.*, so they also recompute when
controlledBy changes, which the old enforcement and value dependencies
missed. Add a unit test for the policy cases, including recommended
policy, which the element tests didn't cover.

[iOS][Actor] Journal PerformActionsFinished and TabObservationController

Log a PerformActionsFinished instant and a TabObservationController
slice from ActorService::OnActCompleted(), matching the entries that
Desktop's ActorKeyedServiceProtoWrapper logs. Both are on the task's
Browser track and record the result code of the first failed action.
TabObservationController also records
skip_async_observation_information, which is always false on iOS since
the screenshot and the APC are always captured.

The slice wraps every RequestTabObservation slice of the batch and ends
after them, so that Perfetto draws the tab observation that follows a
batch of actions as properly nested slices.

Add RecordingJournalObserver, FindJournalDetail() and
IsStrictlyNestedPerTrack() test utilities to verify the order and
nesting of journal entries, since AggregatedJournal::Items() only keeps
the most recent entries.

[Payment Handler] Avoid UAF when synchronously failing window size check

When PaymentRequest.show() is called inside a Document
Picture-in-Picture window, creating and showing the
PaymentRequestDialogView child widget causes
PipChildDialogObserverHelper to synchronously enlarge the PiP window
bounds before ShowDialog() returns. That synchronous bounds change fires
PaymentRequestDialogView::OnWidgetBoundsChanged(), which calls
CheckIfDialogFitsInBrowserWindow().

CheckIfDialogFitsInBrowserWindow will then fail for a PiP window (which
is another bug - crbug.com/573056666) as the auto-resize doesn't include
our 5% safety margin. This failing then synchronously invokes
OnInternalError(), which calls ResetAndDeleteThis(). The PaymentRequest
object is thus destroyed while PaymentRequest::Show() is still on the
call stack.

This CL moves the asynchronous PostTask into
PaymentRequest::OnInternalError() so that all callers avoid synchronous
self-deletion. It also removes the obsolete TODO(crbug.com/483395708)
comment, as there is no point in it now that OnInternalError has to be
async for other callers too.

Fixed: 572422506
Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter="PaymentRequestWindowSizeTest.*"

[NTP] Add NTP component extension scaffolding

Adds the scaffolding for an experimental NTP component extension that
overrides chrome://newtab gated behind `NtpLiteComponentExtension`.

Registration: the extension is added to the component extension
allowlist, to the extensions allowed to use chrome://resources in their
CSP, to ComponentLoader and to ChromeComponentExtensionResourceManager.
Its manifest and page are packed into the browser resources.

NewTabPageExtensionBridge registers an ExtensionConfigProvider,
which supplies loadTimeData, and an ExtensionMojoBinderProvider, which
binds new_tab_page::mojom::PageHandlerFactory (NewTabPageHandler),
searchbox::mojom::PageHandlerFactory (RealboxHandler) and the color
change listener to a per-document handler factory.

Allow calls to GetAssociatedRFHType() for CANCELING navs

When a NavigationThrottle cancels a navigation (e.g. due to the
URLBlocklist policy or mixed content), the NavigationRequest moves to
CANCELING but isn't deleted synchronously (OnStartChecksComplete()
posts a task to OnRequestFailedInternal()). If another pending commit
navigation in the same frame gets its NavigationClient disconnected in
the meantime, DiscardSpeculativeRFHIfUnused() calls
GetAssociatedRFHType() on the CANCELING request and hits a CHECK,
crashing the browser.

This is safe to allow: the CHECK guards against `associated_rfh_type_`
going stale after a navigation moves to its final RenderFrameHost
(READY_TO_COMMIT and later). Unlike the pending commit navigation
above, the canceled navigation in CANCELING hasn't reached that point
and is still owned by the FrameTreeNode, so its `associated_rfh_type_`
is as accurate as for WILL_FAIL_REQUEST, which is already allowed. It
also gives the right answer to DiscardSpeculativeRFHIfUnused(): a
speculative RenderFrameHost still associated with the canceled
navigation is kept rather than discarded.

This is a long-standing crash and a top fatal browser crash on
ChromeOS stable, frequently hit by enterprises using URLBlocklist
policies.

[PageContext] Propagate extraction error enums

Previously, GetAIPageContent and PageContextFetcher only propagated
string error messages to callers on failure, discarding the underlying
AIPageContentExtractionStatus and ScreenshotCaptureStatus enums.

Introduce AIPageContentError and ScreenshotError structs containing both
the status enum and the error message so callers can inspect structured
failure reasons (such as timeouts) and record metrics. Also add kUnknown
= 0 as the default status for uninitialized results and re-version the
corresponding histograms to
OptimizationGuide.AIPageContent.ExtractionStatus2 and
Glic.PageContextFetcher.GetEncodedScreenshot.Status2.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[OptimizationGuide.AIPageContent.ExtractionStatus]=Replaced by OptimizationGuide.AIPageContent.ExtractionStatus2
OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[Glic.PageContextFetcher.GetEncodedScreenshot.Status]=Replaced by Glic.PageContextFetcher.GetEncodedScreenshot.Status2

[iOS] Present customization button IPH bubble after saving NTP photo

Presents the Home customization menu button IPH bubble after a user
saves a custom background photo from the actionable NTP Theme tip card:
- Exposes `-presentCustomizationButtonBubble` on
  `ContentSuggestionsDelegate` and moves its implementation in
  `NewTabPageCoordinator` under `#pragma mark - ContentSuggestionsDelegate`.
- Adds `-didSaveNTPThemeBackgroundPhoto` to
  `ContentSuggestionsViewControllerAudience` and implements it in
  `ContentSuggestionsCoordinator` to forward the request to
  `ContentSuggestionsDelegate`.

[iOS] Add NTPThemeActionableTipView for actionable NTP Theme tip

Adds `NTPThemeActionableTipView` to render the actionable NTP Theme tip
card in the Magic Stack and wires it in
`MagicStackModuleContentsFactory` for
`ContentSuggestionsModuleType::kTipsNTPThemeActionable`:
- Displays circular color palette swatches, preset background image
  swatches, and a photo picker button in a horizontal stack view.
- Updates the selected swatch border and notifies `TipsModuleAudience`
  when a theme swatch or the photo picker button is tapped.
- Observes `prefs::kIosUserUploadedBackground` in
  `TipsMagicStackMediator` to dismiss the actionable tip module once a
  user-uploaded background photo is saved.

More details can be found under the actionable tips section in the WIP
DD go/magic-stack-v2

[ContextualTasks] Refresh tab picker on hover

Opening the composebox context menu in the side panel mounts the
extension tab picker iframe once, and switching or opening browser tabs
while the menu stays mounted does not recreate that frame. Previously,
`TabPickerAppElement` only fetched recent tabs during
`connectedCallback()`, leaving newly opened tabs absent from the flyout
until the user closed and reopened the outer context menu.

Re-fetching recent tabs when hovering over the tab picker trigger or
re-entering an open flyout menu keeps the suggested tab list and most
recent tab indicator up to date without requiring a full menu remount.

[ios] Automatic conversion to TypedProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS

This CL converts most of the ProfileKeyerServiceFactoryIOS sub-classes
to the TypedProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS<Factory, Service> template,
which reduces the boilerplate by automatically generating the methods
GetForProfile(), GetForProfileIfExists() and GetInstance().

The conversion was automated using the script that can be found here:
https://paste.googleplex.com/5101783618289664

The script invocation was:

  $ git grep -l 'public ProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS'|\
    xargs python3 convert.py && git cl format

Only the files that were correctly migrated by the script were kept.
Any files whose migration failed or caused error was either modified
to be converted automatically without error or manually converted.

This CL was uploaded by git cl split.

R=zalmashni@google.com

[chromium-bidi] Include ChromeDriver INFO logs in E2E server log

- Capture ChromeDriver INFO-level browser launch and session commands
  in `chromedriver_e2e.log` on Swarming.
- Previously, `chromedriver_e2e.log` only contained the 4-line
  ChromeDriver startup banner because ChromeDriver defaults to WARNING
  when neither `--log-path` nor `--verbose` is passed
  (crrev.com/c/8589877).
- Pass `--log-level=INFO` to ChromeDriver while keeping verbose mode
  disabled so `COMMAND InitSession`, `Launching chrome: ...`, and
  `RESPONSE InitSession` are written to the log file without console
  output. Chrome's own browser-process stderr remains excluded because
  `--enable-chrome-logs` is not passed.

TAG=agy

3a5399c612f70505697339004aaca072603204c3 [ diff ] 
[metrics] Disable ChromeOS Apps sync in PRE_MigrationRollback_MultiProfile_OneDisabled

In MetricsConsentMigrationRollbackMultiProfileBrowserTest
.MigrationRollback_MultiProfile_OneDisabled, the feature flag
kRestructureMetricsConsentSettings is disabled to test rollback to the
legacy UKM consent logic.

On ChromeOS, the legacy UKM consent logic in
UkmConsentStateObserver::IsUkmAllowedForAllProfiles() allows UKM if
either MSBB or Apps sync (UserSelectableOsType::kOsApps) is enabled for
all profiles. Previously, PRE_MigrationRollback_MultiProfile_OneDisabled
only disabled MSBB for profile_1 without disabling kOsApps, and the test
only passed on ChromeOS because SyncTest created an extra default
browser profile ("test-user") that was signed out of Sync (and thus had
no APPS consent), causing the 3-way consent intersection across profiles
to exclude APPS.

In upcoming patches, SyncTest will be refactored to reuse the default
browser test profile for client 0 instead of leaving it as an extra
signed-out profile. Explicitly disable UserSelectableOsType::kOsApps for
profile_1 on ChromeOS in PRE_MigrationRollback_MultiProfile_OneDisabled
(matching PRE_MigrateSignedIn_AppsDisabled and PRE_MigrationRollback) so
the test does not depend on that extra non-syncing profile.

[ThemeSync] Add click histogram for theme history items.

Each time a user clicks an item in the theme history section of the
NTP customization main bottom sheet, this records two histograms:
- NewTabPage.Customization.ThemeHistory.Click.{PlatformType}. It
  records the item's NtpBackgroundType, split by the platform where
  the theme was originally set.
- NewTabPage.Customization.ThemeHistory.Click.Index. It records the
  index of the clicked item in the list. Index 0 is the default
  theme.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in ios/web and link_to_text

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

Bug: b:501142609
Doc: go/miracleptr-in-containers
DanglingUntriaged-notes: Dangling pointer found by checks after the
rewriting to `raw_ptr` was performed.

1fc4d558d1838722a6211a98b69679aca03cf236 [ diff ] 
Prevent attaching WebRtcAudioRenderer to terminated audio device

WebRtcAudioDeviceImpl::SetAudioRenderer() previously checked only
whether `renderer_` was null before calling
WebRtcAudioRenderer::Initialize() and registering the renderer. If the
audio device had already been terminated via
WebRtcAudioDeviceImpl::Terminate(), or if Terminate() ran on the
signaling thread while Initialize() was executing with `lock_` released,
the renderer retained a raw `source_` pointer to the terminated device
that would not be cleared on subsequent Terminate() calls.

Fix this by:
- Guarding `initialized_` with `lock_` across threads and returning
`renderer_` by value under `lock_` in
WebRtcAudioDeviceImpl::renderer().
- Checking `initialized_` before and after the unlocked
WebRtcAudioRenderer::Initialize() call in SetAudioRenderer(), while
retaining a reference to `this` across Initialize().
- Calling DisconnectSource() and stopping the renderer if Terminate()
intervened during Initialize().

Gardener: Wait for AIM popup focus in WebUILocationBarInteractiveUiTest

In Full WebUI omnibox mode, EscClosesUI() is false on the AIM popup so
VKEY_ESCAPE is handled in the WebUI DOM by the composebox's keydown
listener rather than intercepted in the browser process. Because the AIM
WebContents is prewarmed and ShowWidget() runs synchronously in Full
mode, WaitForAimPopupReady() previously resolved before the widget
became active and before OnPopupShown focused the composebox input,
causing VKEY_ESCAPE in ShowHideAIPopup2/Full to be dropped.

Update WaitForAimPopupReady() to wait until the AIM popup widget is
active and the composebox input matches :focus-visible.

Bug: 572093164
Test: interactive_ui_tests --gtest_filter=WebUILocationBarInteractiveUiTest.ShowHideAIPopup*

parent
dac7438c1a4587964f340f6e9e03615be10cb7fb [ diff ] 
[css-overflow] Fix crash when scroll container status changes

Descendants of an element with scroll-marker-group only generate
::scroll-marker pseudo-elements while that element is a scroll
container. Blink did not treat becoming or ceasing to be a scroll
container as affecting descendants, so the markers were not created or
removed. The layout tree was not reattached either, so when layout
populated the new ::scroll-marker-group it could attach markers that
still had layout objects.

This hits DCHECK(!GetLayoutObject()) in
PseudoElement::AttachLayoutTree().

When scroll-marker-group is not 'none', treat a scroll container change
as descendant-affecting and reattach the layout tree.

This CL removes the TestExpectations entries added in
https://crrev.com/c/8465744.

also parse the URLs entry of the MDM config for the Extensible

only.

Migrate java callers to use DeviceAvailabilityChecker

Decouple biometric availability checks from DeviceAuthenticator
instantiation by exposing
DeviceAuthAvailabilityCheckerBridge.getBiometricAvailabilityStatus() and
gating callers under kDeviceReauthRefactor.

When the flag is disabled, callers continue to take the legacy path via
ReauthenticatorBridge and C++ DeviceAuthenticator. When enabled, callers
check availability statically via DeviceAuthAvailabilityCheckerBridge
without instantiating ReauthenticatorBridge prematurely.

The biggest change is that ReauthenticatorBridge is now only
instantiated if reauth is actually available.

[devtools] Migrate code cache and geolocation web tests to CDP (2/N)

Migrates 4 legacy DevTools web tests from http/tests/devtools/ 1-to-1 to
http/tests/inspector-protocol/ and folds 1 into an existing
inspector-protocol test. These tests only assert on backend
(Blink/V8/content) behavior; the DevTools frontend was just the vehicle
for sending protocol commands and recording traces.

Moved http/tests/devtools/isolated-code-cache/ to
http/tests/inspector-protocol/isolated-code-cache/:
- same-origin-test.js
- same-origin-module-test.js
- cross-origin-test.js
- stale-revalidation-test.js
The tests now record traces with Tracing.start/end directly and print
the raw v8.compile / v8.produceCache (v8.compileModule /
v8.produceModuleCache) trace events through a small shared
resources/code-cache-helper.js, instead of going through the Timeline
panel. Differences in the baselines:
- Full script URLs are printed so that the [A] (127.0.0.1) and [B]
  (localhost) loads can be told apart.
- The frontend-generated "Text details" lines are gone.
- notStreamedReason, cacheKind and line/column numbers are the raw
  values emitted by Blink today. The old baselines were last updated
  in 2021 and were masked by [ Failure ] expectations.
- same-origin-module-test: the last (disk cache) load of the module
  compiles without consuming the code cache, while the old baseline
  expected consumption.
The virtual/threaded suite entries in VirtualTestSuites are updated to
the new location.

Merged into inspector-protocol/emulation/set-geolocation-override.js:
- geolocation-emulation-tests.js. Valid and empty overrides were
  already covered there. The cases that were not yet covered are
  added: invalid parameter type (-32602), out-of-range coordinates
  ("Invalid geolocation"), the previous override being kept after a
  failed call, Emulation.clearGeolocationOverride and the emulated
  position timestamp.

Legacy TestExpectations entries are removed, not carried over, and no
new entries are added for the migrated tests. This drops the flaky
entries for crbug.com/40806190, crbug.com/40814447 and
crbug.com/40217024.

Gardener: Fix event ordering flake in devtools/network/font-face.js

font-face.js logs RequestStarted and RequestFinished events as they
arrive while loading resources/font-face.html. Because font-face.html is
very small, its RequestFinished event races with the renderer parsing
the document and initiating the subresource request (RequestStarted:
used.ttf).

Collect RequestStarted and RequestFinished events separately and sort
them before logging when the test completes, ensuring deterministic
output order while still verifying that used.ttf is requested and
unused.ttf is not.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in ios/

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

As discussed here (https://chromium-review.git.corp.google.com/c/chromium/src/+/8550235/comment/bf30df48_2c7f2af6)
`is_popup_possibly_visible_` flag should explicitly be reset in `AutofillAgent::Reset`.

[BottomSheet] Add baseline tests for sheet geometry and window insets

Establishes baseline characterization tests for BottomSheet geometry,
window insets, and container layout bounds prior to non-E2E wrap-content
adjustments and SSoT inset unification (crbug.com/530492213).

Tests include:
1. Fixed-ratio sheets on mobile (PEEK, HALF, FULL with and
        without Edge-to-Edge insets).
2. Tablet/desktop floating sheets ignoring bottom nav bar
        insets.
3. Window decor vs sheet container layout geometry helper.
4. Landed behavior of wrap-content sheets when edge-to-edge
        insets are 0.

Android: Avoid no-op ScopedServiceBindingBatch in WebContentsImpl

ProcessRankPolicyAndroid::UpdateProcessRank invokes
WebContentsImpl::SetPrimaryPageImportance for all PageNode observer
notifications (e.g. title, favicon, and URL updates), most of which
do not change either the main frame or subframe importance.

Prior to this CL, SetPrimaryPageImportance unconditionally constructed
ScopedServiceBindingBatch before checking whether any
RenderWidgetHostImpl importance actually changed.

This incurred
- two JNI calls
- ScopedJavaGlobalRef allocation,
- launcher-thread batch tasks
- extra samples Android.ChildProcessBinding.BatchScopeDurationOnMainThread

Android 16 x86_64 release emulator, 10x10k trials of no-op
SetPrimaryPageImportance: 10388 ns (batching active) / 4461 ns
(batching inactive) -> 10.3 ns.

32f021c3bd0d401b3d3e9fa6f305a64a2a1607e4 [ diff ] 
spanification: Use base::span in shutdown_signal_handlers_posix

The read and write loops that move a signal number through the
shutdown pipe used to find the next chunk by adding an offset to a
reinterpret_cast'ed pointer. That needed UNSAFE_TODO.

The signal handler now sends the signal number with a single write().
POSIX guarantees that writes of at most PIPE_BUF bytes to a pipe are
atomic, so a write of sizeof(int) bytes is never partial. A
static_assert checks that sizeof(int) <= PIPE_BUF. Only write() and
RAW_CHECK run, so the handler stays visibly async-signal-safe.

The detector thread keeps its read() loop, so that the separate
"error" and "closure" NOTREACHED() messages stay as they were. The
loop now reads into base::byte_span_from_ref(signal) and drops the
bytes already read with subspan(). `signal` is now zero-initialized.

Extract device signals disclaimer test utils

Move the WebUI helpers for the device signals disclaimer into a new
testonly target, device_signals_disclaimer_test_utils, so they can be
shared.

While extracting, a few changes were made:
- WaitForWebContentsLoaded returns testing::AssertionResult instead of
  using ASSERT_TRUE internally, so callers decide whether a failure is
  fatal.
- All helpers check the result of content::WaitForLoadStop() so a failed
  load fails fast instead of polling until the test timeout.
- Drop the log_on_failure parameter and LOG(ERROR) calls; the failure
  context is now part of the returned AssertionResult. Tests that need
  to ignore the logs, use `std::ignore` already.

parent
de098153b97f48cdc88c7b8d33325fc86887f894 [ diff ] 
[Extensions] Prevent accessor execution during global property lookup

When initializing extension bindings on a context's global object,
NativeExtensionBindingsSystem looked up window.chrome using a plain
Get(). If an accessor was defined on the global object, this could
synchronously execute untrusted JavaScript. When deferred script context
initialization occurred during navigation commit, running user script
could synchronously detach the committing frame, leading to use-after-
free issues.

Update GetOrCreateGlobalObjectProperty to inspect own property
descriptors via GetOwnPropertyDescriptor rather than invoking property
getters, ensuring that user script is never executed during bindings
setup and that accessors are not used for extension namespaces.
Additionally, guard against synchronous frame destruction in
ExtensionFrameHelper::ReadyToCommitNavigation using a WeakPtr.

[Journeys] test journey resolution through the public API

Visit resolution is about to be reworked to look up all history
entries with a single query, which starts from the stored journey
rather than an in-memory JourneyRow. Test it through
GetJourneyWithResolvedVisits() and GetAllJourneysWithResolvedVisits()
instead of ResolveJourneyVisits(), so that the same tests cover the new
implementation unchanged.

Also pin down behavior the rework must keep: a URL row with an invalid
URL counts as missing, and when resolving all journeys at once each
journey only sees its own history entries, including when journeys
share a redirect chain's timestamp.

[atmemory] Keep the popup open on layout-induced scrolls

Rotating carousel elements and other dynamic page elements produce
clamping and anchoring scroll events, which closed the popup while
AtMemory query is mid-fetch.

This CL adds the logic to keep the popup open on clamping and
anchoring scroll events. The logic is gated behind a feature flag.

The fix affects only Desktop platforms.

Design doc: go/autofill-popup-layout-shifts

[ios] Automatic conversion to TypedProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS

This CL converts most of the ProfileKeyerServiceFactoryIOS sub-classes
to the TypedProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS<Factory, Service> template,
which reduces the boilerplate by automatically generating the methods
GetForProfile(), GetForProfileIfExists() and GetInstance().

The conversion was automated using the script that can be found here:
https://paste.googleplex.com/5101783618289664

The script invocation was:

  $ git grep -l 'public ProfileKeyedServiceFactoryIOS'|\
    xargs python3 convert.py && git cl format

Only the files that were correctly migrated by the script were kept.
Any files whose migration failed or caused error was either modified
to be converted automatically without error or manually converted.

This CL was uploaded by git cl split.

R=asumaneev@google.com

[searchbox] Serve plural strings over Mojo instead of chrome.send

The composebox components (contextual action menu and entrypoint button)
get the "sharingTabs" plural string through PluralStringProxyImpl, which
uses chrome.send. chrome.send is only available in WebUI renderers, so
these components can't get the string when hosted in an extension page.

This CL adds a small plural_string.mojom.PluralStringProvider interface
in cr_components/search, which holds code shared by the searchbox and
composebox components.

It binds the provider for every host of these components: NTP, omnibox
popup, omnibox everywhere, contextual tasks (WebUI and extension) and
the Lens side panel. The NTP also serves its tab groups module string
("modulesTabGroupsTabsText") through the provider, so it no longer needs
a PluralStringHandler either. Uses the provider in the contextual tasks
extension tab picker so the label is localized.

PluralStringProvider serves only the message names it is created with.
Unknown names and negative counts are reported as bad messages.
